edbDesc: An observed phenomenon in solid solutions or liquid sols that describes the change of an inhomogeneous structure over time, i.e., small crystals or sol particles dissolve, and redeposit onto larger crystals or sol particles. Occurs because larger particles are more energetically favored than smaller particles. This stems from the fact that molecules on the surface of a particle are energetically less stable than the ones in the interior. Ostwald ripening is also observed in liquid-liquid systems, causing diffusion of monomers (i.e. individual molecules or atoms) from smaller droplets to larger droplets due to greater solubility of the single monomer molecules in the larger monomer droplets.
title: Ostwald ripening
description: In a mix of small and large crystals or droplets, the small ones slowly dissolve and their material builds onto the big ones, so the mix gets coarser over time. Wilhelm Ostwald described it in 1896. It is why ice cream turns gritty after weeks in the freezer, and chemists use it on purpose to grow crystals big enough to filter or to make fast photographic film.
effect: small crystals or droplets shrink and feed their material to larger neighbours
usedIn: 'Digesting' precipitates so they can be filtered in chemical analysis
Physical ripening of silver halide grains in photographic emulsions
Ice-cream stabilisers designed to slow it
Controlling particle size in nanoparticle and catalyst making
strength: Slow but steady: ice crystals in stored ice cream grow from about 0.03 mm to over 0.05 mm in a few weeks, big enough to feel on the tongue.
pickWhy: Specific named effect that does a job (growing or coarsening particles) and is controlled in real products.
